subject.title: [Bug]: CLI relay exits silently with code 1 when session lane is blocked — no timeout or busy error surfaced

question: Should source-entrypoint CLI agent dispatch return a terminal session-lane-busy result after the lane wait threshold, and should that use a distinct exit code or the existing generic failure code?
rationale: The bug is real, but the exact user-facing contract affects orchestration scripts and same-session message delivery semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent CLI behavior alone.

options.title: Terminal Busy Result With Clear Contract
options.body: Adopt the linked PR direction, preserve compatibility for CLI identity variants, document or test the stderr/JSON shape, and choose the exit code explicitly.

options.title: Message Only, Existing Exit Code
options.body: Surface a clear stderr/JSON error but keep exit code 1 if maintainers do not want scripts to branch on a new code yet.

options.title: Keep Queueing And Improve Timeout Text
options.body: Reject terminal busy rejection and instead make the eventual timeout path explain the lane wait while preserving current queue semantics.

recommendation.title: Terminal Busy Result With Clear Contract
recommendation.body: Adopt the linked PR direction, preserve compatibility for CLI identity variants, document or test the stderr/JSON shape, and choose the exit code explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: The Gateway-backed CLI relay and current file history point to steipete as the strongest available owner for the CLI/Gateway behavior decision.
